provenance.source_type: general format knowledge derived from parser behavior

applicability: Use when a candidate must be accepted by libarchive's RAR5 reader.
Use when H1 feedback reaches rar5_bid or rar5_read_header but not compressed data parsing.
Do not treat these notes as a complete exploit recipe; they are only container construction constraints.
construction_notes: A RAR5 file begins with the literal signature bytes 52 61 72 21 1a 07 01 00.
After the signature, libarchive reads base blocks. Each base block is encoded as: 4-byte little-endian CRC32, variable-length header size, then header bytes.
The CRC32 is computed over the bytes starting at the encoded header-size field and continuing through the full header payload that is read for that base block.
The base block header payload starts with variable-length header_id followed by variable-length header_flags.

Do not append extra_size or data_size to every base block unconditionally. In libarchive's RAR5 reader, extra_size is read only when HFL_EXTRA_DATA (0x0001) is set, and data_size is read only when HFL_DATA (0x0002) is set.
Known header ids include main=1, file=2, service=3, crypt=4, endarc=5.

A minimal main header with no extra/data flags still includes the main-header archive_flags field after header_id=1 and header_flags=0; for a non-solid, non-volume archive, encode archive_flags=0 as a variable-length integer.
A file header must set HFL_DATA (0x0002) in header_flags when file data follows the header; otherwise the file has no compressed data for archive_read_data to consume.

When HFL_DATA is set on a file header, the file-header bytes after header_id/header_flags begin with a variable-length data_size, then file_flags, unpacked_size, file_attr, compression_info, host_os, name_size, and name bytes. When HFL_EXTRA_DATA is not set, do not insert an extra_size field before data_size.

RAR5 scalar header fields parsed with read_var/read_var_sized must use RAR5 variable-length integer encoding, not fixed little-endian bytes. This includes header_flags, data_size, file_flags, unpacked_size, file_attr, compression_info, host_os, and name_size; fixed little-endian is used only where the parser explicitly reads u32 such as base-block CRC32 or optional time/CRC fields.
compression_info encodes method in bits 7..9 and version in bits 0..5. method=0 is STORE and will use the unstore path; methods 1..5 use the compressed-data path.

The fuzzer usually calls archive_read_next_header first and then archive_read_data. RAR5 compressed block processing happens during archive_read_data through do_unpack -> uncompress_file -> do_uncompress_file -> process_block.
The compressed block bytes follow the file header data area, not as another base block. Its first bytes are a compressed_block_header consumed by process_block.
For libarchive's RAR5 reader, the compressed_block_header byte order is block_flags_u8 first, then block_cksum, then the block-size bytes. Do not write checksum before flags.
In libarchive's compressed_block_header bit layout, bit_size uses bits 0..2, byte_count uses bits 3..5, is_last_block is bit 6, and is_table_present is bit 7 (0x80).

byte_count selects how many additional bytes are used for the compressed block size: byte_count=0 means one following size byte, byte_count=1 means two size bytes, and byte_count=2 means three size bytes.
The compressed block checksum byte is 0x5A XOR block_flags_u8 XOR each block-size byte used by the selected byte_count.
To make process_block call parse_tables, the compressed block header must have is_table_present set in block_flags_u8.
The file header data_size must cover the compressed block header plus the compressed block payload bytes that process_block will read.

In libarchive, process_block reads 4 + cur_block_size bytes after the compressed block header so bit readers can look ahead. Ensure the file data area provides the declared compressed block payload plus at least four following bytes, or the parser can return EOF before parse_tables/do_uncompress_block completes.

avoid: Do not construct arbitrary short byte strings and assume the RAR5 parser will enter compressed data parsing.
Do not put compressed block bytes into the base-block header stream; they belong in the file data area.
Do not use STORE compression when the intended path requires process_block or Huffman table parsing.

positive_output_contract.validation_command_hint: Use a local parser invocation or a lightweight header validator that confirms the candidate is recognized as RAR5 and has a file entry with data.
